title: Ben Johnson: 'We have to play the best we've played all year' on Monday night | Press Conference
headline: Kyle Monangai is out for Monday night at Seattle, Zavier Scott could see more backfield work, and Colston Loveland is on the injury report with what Johnson hopes is a minor issue.
summary: Johnson's press conference centered on the trade for Jeffery Simmons, who is not on the provided roster. Johnson called him a dominant, production-driven defender who will elevate those around him, and said he may not play his usual ~87% snap share in his first week. Johnson said he would count Kyle Monangai (toe) out this week. The team chose not to put him on IR and is hopeful he returns sooner rather than later, but Johnson gave no timetable. Zavier Scott has been active for three weeks and is getting more practice reps. Johnson said he might get more carries and that the team will probably need all three backs given the recent play-time trend. Colston Loveland showed up on the injury report, and Johnson hopes it is minor and expects him to practice. Theo Benedet will start at left tackle. Johnson stressed that Monday night in Seattle against the defending Super Bowl champions requires the team's best play, clean football and sharp communication in a loud stadium, with no turnovers or penalties.

injuries.detail: Toe injury. Johnson would count him out this week, has no timetable, and the team did not use IR. He remains hopeful of a return soon.
On the injury report. Johnson hopes it is minor and expects him to practice Saturday, then will see how it looks.

signals.note: He protects Caleb Williams' blind side on Monday night, which matters for Chicago's pass game against a strong defense.

topics.detail: Chicago traded for Jeffery Simmons, giving up significant draft capital. Johnson expects him to play Monday, possibly below his ~87% snap share in week one, and to boost the whole defense and Dennis Allen's scheme.
Johnson called Seattle a well-coached team strong in all three phases, with a good defense and running game. He said Chicago must play and coach its best and avoid turnovers and penalties.
Johnson called communication the top priority for the loud Monday night road game. He praised Garrett Bradbury as loud and fearless, a key to getting everyone on the same page.
Johnson said the Simmons trade means less high-end draft capital, but he trusts the team's draft-and-develop process. He pointed to practice squad players who are ready to play.

opponent: Seattle Seahawks (Monday night, on the road)

title: Head Coach Mike Macdonald Gives Final Updates Ahead Of Week 8 vs. Bears
headline: Zach Charbonnet is back with a defined plan as a true three-down back, Shaheed is out this week, and Tory Horton gets more work.
summary: Macdonald said the offensive line is being reshuffled, with newly acquired guard Quenton Nelson folded in quickly and Josh Jones at left tackle. He praised Nelson's poise and said he is only a few days into the team. Zach Charbonnet is coming back from injury on an accelerated timeline. Macdonald said there is a specific plan for how much he plays and which plays he gets, though it might waver during the game. He called Charbonnet a three-down back who runs a significant route tree, handles every kind of run and is excellent in pass protection. Rashid Shaheed is out this game and the team will recalibrate next week. Drake Thomas returns and will start at linebacker, though Macdonald said he is not hesitant to play both Thomas and Tyrice Knight together. Macdonald said Tory Horton gets more opportunity and he expects him to take advantage. He declined to explain a possible Monday roster move involving a player referred to as 'JD', saying the transactions would speak for themselves. He was non-committal and positive about Grey Zabel, who was bumped in the line shuffle.
